newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares soften in reporting season lull.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares soften in reporting season lull.

text.p: Singapore shares edged down in early trade on Monday with institutional investors reluctant to commit too heavily during the corporate reporting season, dealers said.
"Once the results are in and they're seen in line with expectations, we'll see the buyers return," said a dealer with a local firm.
Singapore's key Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) had crept down 2.46 points to 2,175.81 at 0255 GMT, with the Business Times-Singapore Regional Index down 4.07 to 1,062.09.
Gainers led losers 106 to 96 with 46.7 million units traded.
Analysts said the STII's fall could continue towards 2,100, but dealers said they were confident such a drop would be short-lived and fuel buy orders to take it back up to 2,200.
"I think fund managers should be using this down trend to buy in and take new positions," said one dealer.
Early trade saw rises for Van Der Horst warrants and common stock up Singapore $0.24 and S$0.20 to S$4.40 and S$5.50 respectively, helping the shares regain some of the ground lost last week.
City Developments led early losers, down S$0.30 to S$13.90.
